passage: Service procedure, Odell dishwashing machine, commercial undercounter model U-2, delime cycle. Delime when the tank heater shows scale or when rinse pressure falls below 18 psi on the gauge, and in any case monthly on hard water. Wear the gloves and eye protection stored with the delimer; the product is acid. Drain the tank using the standpipe, then refill with fresh water and add delimer at 4 ounces per gallon of tank capacity; the U-2 tank holds 5 gallons, thus 20 ounces. Run the pump 15 minutes with the door closed, then inspect through the port: bright metal at the heater indicates completion, gray film calls for a second 10 minute run without new chemical. Never mix delimer with detergent or sanitizer in the tank; chlorine sanitizer contacting the acid releases gas, and the interlock that prevents the sanitizer pump from dosing during delime must be verified annually by a technician, procedure 9-D. After deliming, drain, rinse by filling and draining twice, and refill for service; the first rack washed should be inspected for spotting. Record the delime in the kitchen log with date, initials, and ounces used. Frequent deliming, more than monthly, indicates the water softener needs attention, not more acid; softener service falls under procedure 3-A.
question: How many ounces of delimer does the U-2 tank require?

passage: Rigging guide, Petrel 14 sailing dinghy, section 2: stepping the mast and setting rake. Step the mast on a windless morning if you can; two people make the job safe, one walking the mast up while the other guides the foot into the step and inserts the pivot bolt. Attach the forestay first, then the shrouds, before anyone releases the mast. Set rig tension with the adjustable shroud plates: begin with both shrouds on hole 3 and the forestay just taut. Rake is measured by hoisting a tape on the main halyard and reading the distance from masthead to the top of the transom: the class settles between 21 feet 2 inches and 21 feet 6 inches, with more rake, the smaller number, favored in strong wind for helm balance, and less rake in light air. A weather helm that tires your arm means too much rake; move the shrouds down one hole. Sight the mast from behind for side bend: it must be straight athwartships at rest, and a mast that falls off to one side needs one shroud moved, not both. Tape every ring pin after adjustment; an untaped pin works loose in a season. The boom's gooseneck pin is the last fitting attached and the first removed, and the kicking strap is never left tensioned ashore.
question: What is the smaller of the two class rake measurements?

passage: Programming reference, Fenwick irrigation controller, model FC-8, section 4: zones and schedules. The FC-8 controls eight zones through three independent programs lettered A, B, and C; a zone may belong to any or all programs, and where run times overlap the controller queues zones rather than opening two valves at once, since flow drops below the sprinklers' working pressure with multiple zones open. Assign lawn zones to program A and drip zones to program B as a starting convention; drip runs long and infrequent, lawns short and often, and mixing them in one program forces compromises. Each program takes up to four start times per day; a common error is setting four start times believing they water four zones, when in truth each start time runs the entire program, quadrupling water. Zone run times set to zero exclude the zone from that program. The seasonal adjust dial scales every run time by 10 to 200 percent and is the only control most users need touch between seasons. The rain sensor terminal, when bridged by the supplied jumper, is ignored; remove the jumper when wiring a sensor, or the sensor will be silently defeated, the cause of most soggy lawn complaints after professional installation. Programs survive power failure for 10 years on the lithium cell; the clock survives 48 hours.
question: How many start times per day can each program take?

passage: Care instructions, Bexhill wool blankets, woven goods series. Wash rarely; wool cleans itself of odors with airing, and a blanket hung outdoors on a dry breezy day, out of direct sun, refreshes completely in three hours. When washing is needed, use the machine's wool cycle at 30 degrees or cooler with a neutral wool soap, never biological detergent, whose enzymes digest the fiber itself, thinning the cloth permanently. Spin at 400 revolutions or below. Dry flat across two lines or a rack, shaping while damp; hanging a wet blanket by one edge stretches it beyond recovery, and a tumble dryer, even cool, felts the weave and is the single fastest way to ruin the blanket. Iron only if you must, with steam, on the wool setting, through a cotton pressing cloth. Store clean and bone dry in a breathable cotton bag with cedar; moths seek soiled spots first, and any stain, even invisible, draws them. Never store in plastic, which condenses moisture through seasonal temperature swings. A light pilling on new blankets is loose fiber from finishing, not wear, and lifts away with a fabric comb after the first months. For spills, blot at once with cold water; hot water sets protein stains such as milk or blood.
question: At what maximum temperature should the blanket be machine washed?

passage: Safety data and handling, Grange Chemical, product 88: masonry cleaner, dilute hydrochloric acid 9 percent. Store upright in the original vented container below 90 degrees, away from chlorine bleach products and away from metals; the vapor alone corrodes tools hung above it, a claim adjusters see each spring. Dilution for general brick cleaning: one part product to ten parts water, always adding acid to water, never water to acid, which spatters. Stronger mixes to one part in four are permitted for smoke staining on dense brick only; soft or antique brick is damaged by any strength, test in a hidden spot first. Personal protection: rubber gloves, goggles rather than glasses, and clothing that covers the forearms; a bucket of plain water within reach for immediate rinsing of skin. Application: wet the wall first with plain water, apply the dilution with a fiber brush bottom to top, let it work no longer than five minutes, and rinse top to bottom until runoff no longer fizzes. Never apply to a dry wall, which draws acid deep into the joints, and never use on limestone or marble, which the acid dissolves outright. Neutralize spills with garden lime. First aid for eyes: rinse 15 minutes with water and seek care; do not attempt to neutralize eyes or skin with lime.
question: How much water is mixed with one part product for general brick cleaning?

passage: Setup guide, Tallis stage piano, model SP-6, section 3: connecting for a live venue. Use the balanced quarter inch outputs labeled L and R to the mixing desk; the headphone jack is not a line output, and the buzz reported from small venues traces to that substitution more than any other cause. Set the piano's output level to the detent at three quarters and leave gain staging to the desk. If only one desk channel is free, use the L output alone: the SP-6 sums to mono on that jack when the R jack is empty, a behavior worth demonstrating to skeptical engineers. The pedal input marked DAMPER accepts the supplied half damper pedal; generic switch pedals work but reverse polarity on some brands, making notes sustain until the pedal is pressed, corrected by holding the pedal down during power up. Local speakers switch off automatically when the line outputs detect a connection, overridden under Function, hold 8, for rehearsals needing both. Transpose lives on the panel under Function, hold 3, and resets at power off by design; the setting that survives power off is set differently, through the stored registration slots, of which the SP-6 offers six. Load defaults by powering up with the highest and lowest keys held.
question: Which output should be used when only one desk channel is free?

passage: Winterizing procedure, Halcyon travel trailer, water systems, section 11. Winterize before the first hard freeze; a single night at 20 degrees splits fittings. Begin by draining: open the fresh tank valve, both low point drains, color coded red and blue, and the water heater drain plug, after relieving pressure at the heater's relief valve lever. The water heater holds 6 gallons and drains best warm, not hot. Bypass the heater using the three valve bypass behind the access panel, or antifreeze will pointlessly fill those 6 gallons at a cost of two extra jugs. With drains closed again, connect the pump's winterizing hose to a jug of propylene glycol antifreeze, the pink product sold for plumbing; automotive antifreeze is poisonous in water systems and must never enter the trailer. Run the pump and open each fixture in turn, hot then cold, until pink flows steadily, including the outside shower, the toilet valve, and the city water inlet, which needs its check valve pressed with a pencil until pink appears. Pour a cup of antifreeze into each drain trap. Expect to use two to three gallons in a trailer this size. Leave faucets open over winter and tape a note to the door listing what was done and the date, a courtesy your spring self will thank you for.
question: How much water does the water heater hold?

passage: Reference manual, Corbel document scanner, model DS-90, section 6: feeding and jams. The DS-90 feeds up to 60 sheets of standard paper from the tray; fan the stack and square it before loading, and load face down, top edge first. Mixed sizes feed reliably when aligned to the left guide, the sensor side. Papers below 50 gram weight, onionskin and some receipts, feed singly through the front slot with the thick media lever raised; the lever, despite its name, also relieves roller pressure for thin stock. Staples and clips are the machine's chief enemy: the feed rollers show staple scoring as vertical lines on every scan thereafter, a repair at the roller kit price of 84 dollars, so a staple check is cheaper than any other habit this manual can teach. For a jam, open the top cover fully and pull the sheet in the feed direction, never backward, which flips the separation pad. The pad and both rollers are user replaceable; the software's counter prompts replacement at 100,000 sheets for rollers and 30,000 for the pad, and scans with repeating gray streaks usually mean the pad went unreplaced. Double feed detection uses ultrasound and stops the batch with both sheets held; recover them from the tray side. Clean rollers weekly with the wipes supplied, never alcohol on the pad.
question: How many sheets can the tray feed at once?

passage: Grower's handbook, Marchmont seed company, section on the Verlaine climbing bean. Sow direct after the last frost when soil reaches 60 degrees; seed rots below 55. Plant one inch deep, four inches apart, along a support at least seven feet tall: Verlaine is a true climber and stops setting pods when it runs out of support, so a short trellis costs half the crop. Rows face south by preference, spaced three feet. Water at the root, keeping foliage dry; the variety resists rust well but not perfectly, and wet evening leaves invite it. Pick begins at 62 days from sowing in a warm season and continues eight weeks provided pods are taken young, at six inches, before seeds swell; a single week of neglected fat pods signals the plant to finish, and picking every second day is the whole secret of the long season. Flat brown patches on leaves in late summer are usually sunscald after humid heat, not disease, and pass. Save seed from the earliest podding plants, not the biggest pods: earliness is the trait the variety loses first in careless saving. Leave saving pods until they rattle, then shell and dry a further week indoors. Expect 8 ounces of seed per 10 foot row. The variety was raised at Marchmont in 1969 and is not a hybrid.
question: At what pod length should picking take place?

passage: Emergency procedures card, Loxwood grain elevator, posted at all bin sites. Entry into any bin requires three people: the entrant, the attendant at the hatch who does nothing but tend the lifeline, and the equipment operator who has locked out the auger and holds the key. Zero entry occurs while grain is flowing, without exception; flowing grain buries a standing adult in under 20 seconds, and the pull at knee depth already exceeds what two rescuers can lift. Before entry, lock out the reclaim auger, the sweep auger, and the fill conveyor at their disconnects, each with the entrant's own lock; test each start button after locking. Probe the grain surface from the hatch for crusting: a crusted surface over a void, formed where grain bridged during unloading, collapses under a boot, and is broken up from above with the pole, never by walking on it. The entrant wears the harness clipped to the lifeline at all times, with slack kept under 3 feet by the attendant. Air testing precedes entry after fumigation or when grain is out of condition; the meter must read oxygen above 19.5 percent. If the entrant becomes engulfed to any depth, the attendant calls the rescue number posted below and does not enter; a second person in the grain is a second victim. Rescue tube panels hang in the headhouse.
question: How many people does entry into any bin require?
